args.body:
MEMORANDUM

TO: Engagement Team / Client
FROM: International Trade & Sanctions Practice Group
RE: Analysis of Counterparty Markup of CFIUS National Security Agreement — Risk-Prioritized Memorandum with Recommendations and Counter-Draft Language
DATE: [Current Date]
MATTER: international-trade-sanctions analyze: Analyze Counterparty Markup of CFIUS National Security Agreement

I. PURPOSE AND SCOPE

This memorandum analyzes the counterparty's markup of the draft CFIUS National Security Agreement ("NSA") against the base deal materials, the applicable disclosure schedules and exhibits, and the controlling deal-team instructions. The counterparty accepted most firm-standard provisions but introduced four material deviations. Each deviation is reconciled against (i) the base international trade sanctions materials, (ii) Schedule 3.7 and Schedule 5.2 and Exhibit B, and (iii) the controlling instruction from the most recent deal-team correspondence.

Pursuant to the controlling instruction, the client has agreed to concede the basket conversion, but treats any reduction of the survival period for the core representations as a walk-away issue. Accordingly, this memo risk-prioritizes the deviations and provides counter-draft language for each material change, reflecting client priorities.

Note on scope: A file marked "Unrelated correspondence — administrative file 20" was misfiled into the matter folder and concerns a different client engagement. It has not been relied upon in preparing this memorandum.

II. SUMMARY OF MATERIAL DEVIATIONS AND RISK RANKING

The counterparty markup introduces four material deviations. Consistent with the controlling deal-team instruction, each is ranked below by risk and by the client's stated negotiation posture:

| Priority | Deviation | Client Posture | Recommended Action |
|----------|-----------|----------------|--------------------|
| 1 — WALK-AWAY | Limitation-period reduction shortens survival for core representations (contradicts Exhibit B) | Walk-away | Reject; hold to Exhibit B survival matrix |
| 2 — HIGH | Indemnification cap silently reduced (shifts retained liabilities per Schedule 5.2) | Negotiate up | Restore cap in line with firm standard / Schedule 5.2 |
| 3 — MEDIUM | MAE carve-outs for regulatory action (intersects Schedule 3.7 pending inquiries) | Reconcile | Narrow carve-outs to disclosed inquiries only |
| 4 — CONCEDE | Basket converted from deductible to tipping basket | Concede (per client) | Accept, confirm consequential drafting |

III. DETAILED DEVIATION ANALYSIS AND COUNTER-DRAFT LANGUAGE

DEVIATION 1 — SURVIVAL-PERIOD REDUCTION (WALK-AWAY ISSUE)
Risk: HIGHEST. This is the controlling client walk-away issue.

The counterparty proposes to add a new limitation period that shortens survival for the core representations (including the fundamental representations). This directly contradicts the survival matrix set forth in Exhibit B to the base materials, which fixes the survival periods that bind both parties. Because the scheduled exhibits and their survival matrix "control over general statements in the base materials," the counterparty's shortened limitation period must be rejected.

Recommendation: Reject the proposed limitation-period reduction in its entirety. Hold firmly to the Exhibit B survival matrix. This is a walk-away issue and should not be conceded or traded.

Counter-draft language (to replace the counterparty's proposed limitation period):

"The representations and warranties of the Parties shall survive the Closing for the respective periods set forth in Exhibit B. No claim for breach of any representation or warranty may be asserted after the applicable survival period set forth in Exhibit B has expired, except that (i) claims for fraud, willful breach, or breach of the fundamental representations shall survive until the expiration of the applicable statute of limitations, and (ii) any extension, modification, or waiver of the survival periods set forth in Exhibit B must be in writing and signed by both Parties. For the avoidance of doubt, the survival matrix in Exhibit B shall control and may not be amended or shortened except by written agreement of both Parties."

Rationale: This preserves the Exhibit B matrix, keeps the fundamental-representation carve-outs intact, and prevents the counterparty's shortened limitation period from eroding the core protections.

DEVIATION 2 — INDEMNIFICATION CAP SILENTLY REDUCED / RETAINED LIABILITIES SHIFT
Risk: HIGH.

The counterparty silently reduces the indemnification cap. This change intersects Schedule 5.2, which lists retained liabilities that the indemnification provisions presently cover. Reducing the cap below the value covered by Schedule 5.2 would silently shift those retained liabilities back to the client, undermining the negotiated allocation of risk.

Recommendation: Reject the reduced cap and restore the cap to the firm-standard level reflected in the base materials. If the counterparty insists on a cap reduction, require a corresponding carve-out of the Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities from the reduced cap (i.e., retained liabilities remain fully indemnified notwithstanding any cap).

Counter-draft language (for the indemnification/cap provision):

"The aggregate liability of the Sellers under the indemnification obligations in this Agreement shall not exceed [BASE MATERIALS CAP AMOUNT], except that (i) the cap shall not apply to liabilities arising from the retained liabilities set forth in Schedule 5.2, (ii) the cap shall not apply to fraud, willful breach, or breach of the fundamental representations, and (iii) the cap shall not apply to any liability that is otherwise excluded by the express terms of this Agreement. For the avoidance of doubt, the retained liabilities listed on Schedule 5.2 shall be indemnified in full and shall not be subject to, or reduced by, any cap or other limitation on the Sellers' aggregate indemnification liability."

Rationale: This restores the cap to firm standard and affirmatively protects the Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities from being silently shifted to the client by a cap reduction.

DEVIATION 3 — MATERIAL ADVERSE EFFECT (MAE) CARVE-OUTS FOR REGULATORY ACTION
Risk: MEDIUM.

The counterparty adds carve-outs to the definition of Material Adverse Effect for "regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter." This is problematic because Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that are the precise kind of regulatory action at issue. Adding a blanket MAE carve-out for regulatory action would effectively strip the MAE protections for the very matters disclosed on Schedule 3.7, and would also sweep in future, undisclosed regulatory actions.

Recommendation: Narrow the carve-out so that it applies only to the specific, disclosed regulatory inquiries listed on Schedule 3.7 and only for the period reflected in the disclosure. Reject any carve-out that extends to future or undisclosed regulatory actions.

Counter-draft language (for the MAE definition):

"'Material Adverse Effect' means any change, event, occurrence, or condition that has had, or would reasonably be expected to have, a material adverse effect on the business, assets, liabilities, financial condition, or results of operations of the Company, taken as a whole. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the following shall not, individually or in the aggregate, be deemed to constitute, or be taken into account in determining whether there has been, a Material Adverse Effect: ... (x) any regulatory inquiry, investigation, or action, but only (A) to the extent it arises out of the specific pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7 and (B) solely with respect to the period and scope disclosed on Schedule 3.7. For the avoidance of doubt, no regulatory action that arises after the date of this Agreement or that is not expressly disclosed on Schedule 3.7 shall be excluded from the definition of Material Adverse Effect."

Rationale: This bounds the MAE carve-out to the specifically disclosed inquiries on Schedule 3.7, prevents a walk-away of MAE protection for future or undisclosed regulatory action, and honors the schedule-exception rule that scheduled exceptions control over general statements.

DEVIATION 4 — BASKET CONVERTED FROM DEDUCTIBLE TO TIPPING BASKET (CONCEDED)
Risk: LOW (per controlling client instruction).

The counterparty converts the indemnification basket from a deductible (under which losses below the threshold are borne entirely by the indemnitee) to a tipping basket (under which, once the threshold is crossed, the entire amount including amounts below the threshold becomes recoverable). Pursuant to the controlling deal-team instruction, the client has agreed to concede this conversion.

Recommendation: Accept the basket conversion as conceded. However, confirm the consequential drafting so that the tipping-basket mechanics are internally consistent (i.e., that (i) the threshold operates as a true tipping threshold, (ii) there is no double-counting, and (iii) any basket-based exclusions align with the indemnification scope in Deviation 2 above).

Counter-draft language (for the basket provision):

"The Parties shall have no liability for indemnification claims under this Agreement unless and until the aggregate amount of all losses that would otherwise be indemnifiable exceeds [BASKET AMOUNT], at which point the Sellers shall be liable for the full amount of such losses from the first dollar (a 'tipping basket'), subject to the cap and any exclusions set forth in the indemnification provisions above. Claims for fraud, willful breach, or breach of the fundamental representations shall not be subject to the basket."

Rationale: This confirms the conceded tipping-basket mechanics and ensures consistency with the cap and carve-outs addressed in Deviation 2.

IV. CONCLUSION AND NEXT STEPS

The counterparty's markup contains four material deviations. Per the controlling instruction, the basket conversion is conceded (Deviation 4). The survival-period reduction (Deviation 1) is a walk-away issue and must be rejected outright; the indemnification cap reduction (Deviation 2) must be restored to protect the Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities; and the MAE carve-outs (Deviation 3) must be narrowed to the specific Schedule 3.7 disclosed inquiries. Recommended counter-draft language for each deviation is set forth above.

Next steps: (1) Return counter-draft to counterparty with Deviations 1–3 marked as rejected/revised and Deviation 4 accepted; (2) confirm the Exhibit B survival matrix remains unchanged; (3) verify Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities remain fully indemnified notwithstanding any cap; and (4) monitor the status of the two pending regulatory inquiries on Schedule 3.7.

Prepared by: International Trade & Sanctions Practice Group
